subject.title: Bug: channel stop timeout leaves channel permanently dead — running: true with stale store entries

question: Should timed-out channel stops use a generic forced-recovery contract, or should transport owners such as Telegram provide explicit task/socket disposal before the gateway releases lifecycle ownership?
rationale: The reported task can remain live after abort; choosing between generic store cleanup and transport-specific destruction determines whether recovery risks concurrent channel ownership or continues to wedge.

options.title: Define explicit transport recovery ownership
options.body: Require the affected channel owner to expose a bounded disposal/recovery hook, then let the gateway release task state only after that contract is satisfied.

options.title: Use gateway-only forced map cleanup
options.body: Clear the gateway lifecycle maps after timeout and accept the risk that an unresponsive old task may overlap the new task.

options.title: Escalate to a process recovery boundary
options.body: Keep task ownership intact and add a bounded operator-visible gateway restart escalation after repeated failed channel recoveries.

recommendation.title: Define explicit transport recovery ownership
recommendation.body: Require the affected channel owner to expose a bounded disposal/recovery hook, then let the gateway release task state only after that contract is satisfied.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged recovery work is the closest current-main implementation on the affected restart path.
